finding_A_the_new_correlation_assertion.question: does it prove the card's events-and-cost-bound-to-the-Run property, does it prove only the identity half, and is the remaining disclosure accurate and narrow?
finding_A_the_new_correlation_assertion.answer: It proves the identity half, and it proves it with production code on the line, not with wording. The worker is started with rt.Spec{RunID: domain.Str(run,'id'), TaskID: domain.Str(taskA,'id'), Epoch: epoch} where epoch is read from the claimed Run's lease_epoch (:452-455, and createRuntimeRun at internal/domain/runtime.go:41-48 makes lease_epoch an int64, so the float64 cast is the real value and not the silent fallback to 1); the row then requires the settled journal's Spec to equal all three, one artifact, at least one stream with a non-empty OutHash, and a ledger reservation whose provider_request_id is exactly 'fixture-dispatch/'+that run id with no other reservation for the Run.
finding_A_the_new_correlation_assertion.not_tautological_but_partly_echo: The ledger clause is a genuine cross-check: the reservation is written by the service (internal/domain/budget_scopes.go:136) and read back through the service's own BudgetUsage, which filters rows by json_extract(body,'$.run_id')=? (internal/domain/budget_usage.go:24), so no row unrelated to the Run can enter the count - the two things that could make it pass wrongly (a run-scoped leak, an unkeyed key) are excluded by the query and by the exact key comparison, and M22 (which sets run_id nil and the key to 'unkeyed') kills the row. The journal clause is weaker: Worker.Wait returns w.Read() (adapters/runtime/runtime_windows.go:221-236), which marshals the in-memory journal rather than reading journal.json, so rj.Spec is the value Start stored at :152 echoed back to the caller. It is not vacuous - M21 (journal built without the Spec it was given) kills it, in all five of my runs - but as written the row does not prove the identity survived a durable round trip. I checked that separately myself: the persisted record at .local/w0501-run/runbound/runbound/journal/journal.json carries spec.run_id e719e9393770aa4fda4d3bcc8e2a38a6, spec.task_id 61f46eabe584499abfaf40e81fd2311b, epoch 1, state SETTLED, one artifact (output.txt, sha256:8419e16b969..., 20 bytes) and one stream with a stdout hash, and the run id is a 32-hex domain id, not the fixture-local 'run-copy-1' the adapter phase uses. The cheap strengthening is to read it back through runtime.Reconcile(directory) instead of trusting the echo.
finding_A_the_new_correlation_assertion.what_it_does_not_prove: not the domain event ledger (the service refuses a report with no trusted observation, which the suite asserts as its own row), not cost beyond a proven-zero fixture hold, and not recovery of the identity after a worker restart. The card's clause is 'events/cost bound to the Run'; what is bound here is one journal record and one ledger key to one Run identity.
finding_A_the_new_correlation_assertion.disclosure_accurate_and_narrow: Substantially yes, with one imprecision. Measured: the only non-test production callers of rt.Start in the tree are ops/runtime/main.go:63 (a standalone tool) and this check program; internal/domain contains none. The service does launch a worker from inside itself - RuntimeCoordinator.dispatchGate then rt.StartBridge at internal/domain/runtime_coordinator_windows.go:421-499 - but that is the AppContainer bridge, which refuses unless the profile says backend native-offline and model none (adapters/runtime/bridge_windows.go:147-150 and the frozen-build hash comparison at :168-169) and unless an exact qualification marker matches the Run id and lease epoch (internal/domain/runtime_dispatch.go:50-51, 422 GATE_FAILED). The one place a Run-keyed rt.Start exists in domain code is the LIVE qualification test internal/domain/orchestration_agent_test.go:182, which needs an authorized auth.json and the pinned binary. So attributing the remaining half to the runtime qualification gate is right and it is narrow. The imprecision is in the source comment at w0501.go:437-439, 'nothing in this tree launches the adapter from the service', which is false as literally stated: the coordinator launches the bridge from the service, and an accepted domain test launches this very adapter under a domain Run id. The receipt's own sentence for the same block, check_results.not_verified[9] (W0501-RUN-EVENT-AND-COST-CORRELATION), does not make that absolute claim; it says what is left is the service launching the adapter on its own and names the gate, which I confirmed.
